conviction_note: This release carries the first FY27 guide. Two counterparties put that guide's inputs below the street's $3.15: Intel's 2027 PC-unit view (-10%) is about twice HP's own planning assumption (mid-single-digit decline), and HP's calendar-Q3 units were -31% against its own 'high-teens' industry framing. Pointing the other way: the stock is already down 17% since Intel spoke, Lenovo's PC revenue held at +15% with a 7.1% margin, and the short base is building. The findings sum to -2.2; the scaled number is -1.1 (p_up 43 x abs 8.0) because most of the negative overlaps the drawdown and the 12-point put skew already in the price.

Consensus $0.74 / revenue $15.30B (Yahoo, 13 and 12 analysts: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HPQ/analysis); $0.75 / $15.47B (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-16: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/HPQ/23239). Whisper $0.90. FY27 street: EPS $3.15 (range 2.75-3.54, 18 analysts), revenue $59.97B (+0.4%), from Yahoo only, so FY27-dependent findings are capped. EW's article quotes the GAAP range ($0.74-0.84) as if it were non-GAAP; the non-GAAP guide is $0.69-0.79.

expectations.real_bar: An EPS beat is assumed (whisper $0.90). To rise, the stock needs a FY27 EPS guide with a midpoint at or near the street's $3.15, despite non-recurring FY26 tariff refunds and Intel's -10% 2027 unit view, plus confirmation that Q4 was the Personal Systems margin trough.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY27 EPS $3.15 (range 2.75-3.54, 18 analysts; unchanged from 30 and 60 days ago), revenue $59.97B (+0.4%) (Yahoo https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HPQ/analysis)
next_guide.company_current_guide: None for FY27. The 2026-09-21 8-K withholds FY27 guidance and assumes calendar-2027 industry PC units fall roughly mid-single digits (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000047217/000114036126037170/ef20082499_form8k.htm). On the Q3 call: input costs rise in FY27 at a slower rate, and the PS margin goes back to its long-term range as quickly as possible.
next_guide.basis: The first FY27 guide is likely to come in below the $3.15 street midpoint, for four reasons. FY26's $3.19-3.29 includes $0.19 of tariff refunds. Intel's 2027 unit view (-10%) is about twice HP's own assumption. TrendForce has PC DRAM still rising 13-18% in 4Q26, with Korean suppliers cutting PC DRAM output by more than 20% in 2027. And last year HP opened FY26 at $2.90-3.20, below the street. Against that: management says Q4 is the margin trough, and Lenovo held a 7.1% PC margin.

findings.finding: Intel (HP's main CPU supplier) said on 2026-10-29 that industry PC units fall about 12% in 2026 and about 10% in 2027. HP's own 8-K of 2026-09-21 assumed calendar-2027 units decline only 'roughly mid-single-digits'. Yet the street's FY27 EPS ($3.15) and revenue (+0.4%) have not moved in 30 or 60 days, so HP's first FY27 guide is built on a unit outlook about twice as bad as HP last said.
findings.link: Intel supplies the x86 CPUs in most HP PCs; Intel's client unit view is a read on the same end market and on OEM order books, including HP's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When HP issued its first FY26 guide (2025-11-25, $2.90-3.20 against a higher street), the stock fell 1.4% (baseline). The 2026-09-21 8-K with the mid-single-digit unit assumption cost -2% intraday (https://finviz.com/news/393837/hp-shares-fall-2-as-company-anticipates-pc-market-contraction-in-2027).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has partly priced it: -9.5% on 2026-10-30 and -17% over six sessions. The sell-side has not: FY27 EPS sits at $3.15, the same as 30 and 60 days ago. If estimates had absorbed Intel's view, the FY27 average would have fallen and revenue would show a decline, not +0.4%. The open question is whether HP's guide resets the estimates.
findings.independence: HP's own 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000047217/000114036126037170/ef20082499_form8k.htm) gives the mid-single-digit comparison. The Intel drop and its spillover to HP and Dell are reported independently (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nyse/hpq/news/why-up-down/why-hp-hpq-shares-are-sliding-today). Shares its guide target with the FY27 guide-arithmetic finding below, but rests on a different fact.

findings.finding: FY26 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $3.19-3.29 includes $0.19 of tariff refunds ($0.08 in Q4), which leaves an underlying base of about $3.00-3.10. The street's FY27 $3.15 therefore assumes underlying EPS growth in a year when Intel sees units -10%, management expects input costs to keep rising, and PS margins start below their 5-7% range. Last year HP opened FY26 at $2.90-3.20, below the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First-guide prints: 2025-11-25 -1.4% close to close, despite an 'up 12% over the following week' path (https://www.aol.com/articles/hp-inc-earnings-preview-wall-183506855.html). 2025-02-27 -6.82% and 2025-05-28 -8.27%, both guide-led cuts (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Yahoo's FY27 average ($3.15, up from $3.00 90 days ago) moved up with the FY26 raise and has not come back down. If the market expected the refunds to roll off into a lower FY27, the estimate would have drifted down after the 8-K and after Intel. The put skew suggests the options market expects something like this, so the size is held down. FY27 consensus has only one source, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: The refund amounts come from the FQ3 press release (https://finviz.com/news/385926/hp-inc-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results). The FY27 street figure comes from Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HPQ/analysis). Shares the transcript with the Q4 trough claims.

findings.finding: IDC (2026-10-08) has HP calendar-Q3 PC units at 10.3M, -30.9% y/y, with share down from 19.1% to 16.5%, against an industry -20.1%; Gartner also has HP at -30.9%. HP's Q4 guide (Aug-Oct) assumed industry units down 'high-teens' and revenue up y/y. The street's FQ4 revenue of $15.3-15.47B (+4.5-5.7%) needs PS revenue of about +8% on units of about -28%, which means PS ASP up about 50% against about 40% in FQ3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HP has beaten revenue every quarter of FY26 (FQ3 PS revenue $11.8B against about $10.5B consensus), and the stock still fell on those prints (baseline -1.88% and -2.92%).
findings.why_not_priced: The street's FQ4 revenue average has not fallen: $15.30B on Yahoo, $15.47B on EW. If the -31% unit figure had been carried into models, the FQ4 average would sit near or below the year-ago $14.64B. IDC blames earlier pull-ins, so the sell-in drop may overstate HP's own fiscal-quarter sell-in. That is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Gartner's 2026-10-12 release also has HP at -30.9% (https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-10-12-gartner-says-worldwide-pc-shipments-declined-22-point-4-percent-in-third-quarter-of-2026-as-component-cost-inflation-raised-asps; fetch 403, snippet only). Lenovo's revenue print (finding below) points the other way, which is why this proxy is sized below it.

findings.finding: Lenovo, the #1 PC vendor, reported on 2026-11-19 for July-September, after HP last spoke. IDG revenue was +15% y/y to $17.4B with operating margin 7.1%, described as 'well maintained', while its units fell 22.6% in IDC's data. Price is offsetting units and PC margins are holding at the market leader.
findings.link: Same product and channel: Lenovo (23.8% unit share) and HP (16.5%) are #1 and #2 in IDC's 3Q26 table, and Lenovo's fiscal Q2 overlaps two of HP's three FQ4 months. HP's FQ4 PS is about 75% of revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HP's PS revenue beat by about 12% in FQ3, the margin came in at 4.6% (below range, as guided), and the stock fell 2.9%. Good PS revenue alone has not lifted it.
findings.why_not_priced: HPQ's 5-day change is -0.44%, so Lenovo's release did not move it; the stock still sits near its post-Intel low. If the market had read Lenovo as clearing HP's revenue and margin risk, HPQ would have recovered part of the Intel gap. Lenovo's IDG includes phones, which dilutes the read.
findings.independence: Unit figure from IDC (https://idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/idc-pc-tracker-3q26). The margin figure is from the 36Kr analysis via search (https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4076212792711041).

findings.finding: TrendForce (2026-11-11) sees PC DRAM contract prices +13-18% q/q in 4Q26, down from +18-23% in 3Q26. That supports HP's claim that Q4 is the margin trough. But costs are still rising, OEM and North American channel finished-goods inventory is building, OEMs are cutting 4Q26-1Q27 SSD and DRAM procurement, and Korean suppliers plan to cut PC DRAM output by more than 20% in 2027. Net: a constrained FY27 cost line and a weak FQ1 sell-in.
findings.link: Memory and storage are about 35% of HP's PC bill of materials (HP CFO, reported https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/hp-says-memory-costs-doubled-to-35-percent-of-pc-build-materials-in-one-quarter); TrendForce tracks the contract prices HP pays.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Memory-cost commentary drove the -2.92% (FQ3) and -1.88% (FQ2) reactions to EPS beats (https://invezz.com/news/2026/08/27/hp-stock-slides-5-as-memory-costs-pressure-pc-margins/).
findings.why_not_priced: The decelerating price increase and the inventory build cut in opposite directions. The channel-inventory point is new since HP last spoke, and its effect on HP's FQ1 sell-in guide ($14.76B street) has not shown in the estimates, which are flat over 30 days.
findings.independence: The deceleration matches HP's own 'slower rate' language in the Q3 transcript. The inventory build matches IDC's 'channels worried about too much inventory' (https://idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/idc-pc-tracker-3q26).

findings.finding: Expectations have been reset: HPQ is $28.59, 21% below its post-FQ3 high of $36.23 and back at the level it fell to after FQ3. Most of that came from a -17.1% six-session slide (S&P -1.4%) set off by Intel's warning. A FY27 guide merely in line, or 'Q4 trough confirmed' with sequential margin improvement, meets a bar the price has already lowered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the soft FY26 guide in 2025-11 the stock fell 1.4% on the day, then rose about 12% over the following week (https://www.aol.com/articles/hp-inc-earnings-preview-wall-183506855.html). On 2026-11-04 the CEO-appointment news lifted it as much as 6.9% intraday (https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/sci-tech/2026-11-04-hp-taps-ex-gsk-boss-emma-walmsley-as-ceo-amid-sales-crunch/).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is priced by definition. The question is whether the 12-point put skew and the 8% implied move overstate the downside after a 17% drawdown. Spot is still about 10% above the mean target ($26.07), so the reset is not complete, and the size is kept small.
findings.independence: Intel-driven gap documented separately (https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-hp-inc-hpq-stock-down-9-49-today-24286/). Mean target from a Benzinga snippet (https://www.benzinga.com/stock/HPQ/ratings).

findings.finding: The real EPS bar is above consensus: the whisper is $0.90 against $0.74-0.75 consensus and a $0.69-0.79 guide, after two straight 20% EPS beats ($0.83 against $0.69, $0.86 against $0.72). Both of those beats were sold (-2.92%, -1.88%), so a beat to the low $0.80s probably meets the whisper and does not move the stock up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last four EPS surprises +0.8%, +5.6%, +20.3%, +20.0% (Yahoo). Reactions -1.40%, +0.05% (the 2026-02-24 print; the baseline also lists a 2026-02-03 event at +4.32%), -1.88%, -2.92%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the whisper is the market's own expectation. It is filed because the published consensus understates the bar the stock is held to, and a judge sizing against $0.75 would overrate an EPS beat.
findings.independence: Earnings history from Yahoo (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/HPQ/analysis); reactions from the baseline.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 76.42M shares (8.47% of shares outstanding, 5.91 days to cover) on 2026-10-30, from 73.09M (4.60 days) on 2026-09-30, while the 25-delta skew sits at +12.3 vol points to puts. A building, moderately sized short base meets a guide that is 'less bad than Intel'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No squeeze has been recorded on HPQ prints in the baseline. The largest up-reaction is +4.57% (2025-08-27).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest and skew are visible to anyone, so this is not hidden information. It sets how lopsided the reaction can be. Under 10% short with about 6 days to cover is not crowded, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Skew from the sealed baseline (yahoo options, 2026-11-24 18:12 UTC). Sept 30 figures confirmed by a second aggregator (search snippet, massive.com).

findings.finding: Mid-quarter: on 2026-11-04 HP named Emma Walmsley (ex-GSK) CEO effective 2027-01-04, with interim CEO Broussard becoming chair. The FY27 guide on this call is therefore set by an interim team for an incoming CEO, which plausibly favours a conservative, beatable range or a framework rather than a point estimate (inference).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior guide set by an outgoing team in the baseline. The appointment itself lifted the stock up to 6.9% intraday on 2026-11-04.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is public. How it affects the guide is inference only. If the market expected a kitchen-sink guide, FY27 estimates would have come down after 2026-11-04; they did not ($3.15 for 30 days).
findings.independence: none (inference from the appointment; the release gives no guidance, per the same document)

outside_window.finding: HP's PS president Ketan Patel speaks at the UBS conference on 2026-12-01, with Wells Fargo on 12-07 and Barclays on 12-10. These are the next chances to clarify the FY27 guide.
Walmsley takes over as CEO on 2027-01-04; any strategic reset or rebased targets come after the window.

rejected_candidates.detail: Folded into the FY27 guide-arithmetic finding: the refunds matter only through their roll-off from the FY27 base. Inside the quarter they are within the guided range.

rejected_candidates.detail: Other sources show Morgan Stanley at Underweight throughout 2026 (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/hp-s-unit-and-margin-pressures-not-factored-in-by-the-stock-s-multi-year-valuation-highs-says-morgan-stanley/cZMRjXfRBIc), and the page's dates are internally inconsistent. baseline_tension: The negative guide findings agree with the 12-point put skew and the -15% run-in, so they are largely priced. The positive items (Lenovo, the reset price, a building short base) cut against the skew. Net, the lean is only mildly negative, and p_up sits close to 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning, the skew agrees): Intel counterparty finding cut from -1.5 to -1.0, because the 17% drawdown and the put skew already carry most of it.
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): FY27 consensus has one source (Yahoo), so the FY27 guide finding is capped from -2.0 to -1.5.

Lesson 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a direct series): the IDC/Gartner unit finding cut from -1.0 to -0.6, because Lenovo's directly reported revenue (+15%) and HP's own FQ3 price/units history point the other way.
Lesson 5 (inference small): CEO-transition finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism' and lesson 3: p_up moved from 42 to 43, abs_move left at 8.0; expected_move -1.28 to -1.12.
Lessons 1 and 2 left the EPS-whisper finding (beats sold) and the treatment of tariff refunds as non-findings unchanged; both were already applied in the draft.
